from.place: Statement, 'Every map involved was normalized by the Kummer generator', and Proof, the inverse diagonal identification: comparison of the normalized vector-bundle map used at the normal-bundle endpoint

title: Finite-level site comparison of normalized vector-bundle integration
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient data of [def-pur-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$ and arbitrary $n\geq1$. Let $S$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $\pi:V\to S$ be a vector bundle of constant rank $d\geq0$ with zero section, in the sense of [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. No separatedness of $S\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is assumed. For every scheme $T$ over $S$ write $C_T=\nu_T^*:D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)\to D^+(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ for comparison pullback [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. Use constant discrete module sheaves and their ordinary etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], ordinary etale compact supports [def-amb-etale-compact-support], pro-etale compact supports [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], derived pullback and tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and the transported constructible exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Choose any $r\geq1$ with $\ell^r A=0$ and put
$$L_T=\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{\ell^r,T}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}A_T,\qquad L_T(d)=L_T^{\otimes_A d}.$$
Here $\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{\ell^r,T}$ is the sheaf of units $z$ satisfying $z^{\ell^r}=1$, with powers giving the $\mathbf Z/\ell^r$ action. The ordinary etale twist is as in [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]; the pro-etale twist remains the specified inverse-limit twist of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Let
$$\tau_T:C_TL_T\xrightarrow{\sim}A_T(1)$$
be the comparison induced by the inverse of projection from the roots-of-unity tower after scalar extension, as in [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map]. The maps $\tau_T$ and their tensor powers commute with inverse image along every morphism $w:T'\to T$ over $S$, identifying $Lw^*A_T(d)$ with $A_{T'}(d)$.

For $q:P=\mathbf P^1_S\to S$, write $b_q^e,h_q^e,t_q^e$ for the ordinary etale decomposition, Kummer class of $\mathcal O_P(1)$, and trace of [def-amb-p1-trace]. On the pro-etale site let $h_q^p:A_S\to Rq_{p,*}A_P(1)[2]$ be the adjoint of $A_P\to i_*A_S\xrightarrow{c_{H,A}}A_P(1)[2]$, where $i:S\hookrightarrow P$ is the infinity hyperplane $H$, with $\mathcal O_P(H)=\mathcal O_P(1)$, and $c_{H,A}$ is the supported class of [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map]. Let $b_q^p$ be the map with components the shifted twisted unit and $h_q^p$. With $\beta_q:C_SRq_{e,*}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_{p,*}C_P$ the canonical counit-mate comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate], and $\tau$ and the finite direct-sum identifications understood, the actual maps satisfy
$$\beta_q C_S(b_q^e)=b_q^p.$$
In particular $b_q^p$ is invertible; with $t_q^p=\operatorname{pr}_2(b_q^p)^{-1}$ one has
$$t_q^p\beta_q=C_S(t_q^e),\qquad t_q^p h_q^p=1.$$
For $j:\mathbf A^1_S\hookrightarrow P$, the canonical comparison $C_Pj_!^e\cong j_!^p C_{\mathbf A^1_S}$ identifies the counit $j_!j^*\to1$ on the two sites. Together with $\beta_q$ it carries the restriction of $t_q^e$ by $Rq_*j_!\to Rq_*$ to the corresponding restriction of $t_q^p$.

Let $t_\pi^e:R\pi_!^e L_V(d)[2d]\to A_S$ be the vector-bundle integration of [def-amb-vector-integration], constructed on trivializing opens by ordered composition of these restricted projective-line traces [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace]. On the pro-etale site form $t_\pi^p$ by the same local integrations using $t_q^p$, with the specified twists and canonical compact-support composition comparisons. These local maps agree on overlaps and define a global morphism. For the projective completion $V\xrightarrow{j_V}\overline V\xrightarrow{\overline\pi}S$, define the compact-support comparison to be the composite of the counit-mate proper direct-image comparison with the extension-by-zero comparison $e_{j_V}$ of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]:
$$C_SR\overline\pi_{e,*}j_{V!}^e\xrightarrow{\beta_{\overline\pi}}R\overline\pi_{p,*}C_{\overline V}j_{V!}^e\xrightarrow{R\overline\pi_{p,*}(e_{j_V})}R\overline\pi_{p,*}j_{V!}^pC_V.$$
Denote the resulting map by
$$\beta_\pi:C_SR\pi_!^e\xrightarrow{\sim}R\pi_!^p C_V$$
It identifies the actual global maps:
$$t_\pi^p\beta_\pi=C_S(t_\pi^e).$$
For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ (bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude, the ordinary etale version of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]), the same comparisons identify the canonical compact-support tensor projection maps, and the integration maps
$$a_K^e:R\pi_!^e(\pi_e^*K\otimes_A^L L_V(d)[2d])\xrightarrow{\operatorname{PF}}K\otimes_A^LR\pi_!^e L_V(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{1\otimes t_\pi^e}K$$
and $a_{C_SK}^p$ defined by the corresponding pro-etale formula. If $\eta_K^e$ is the adjoint transpose of $a_K^e$ under the ordinary etale compact-support adjunction, and $\eta_{C_SK}^p$ is the transpose of $a_{C_SK}^p$ under the bounded etale-origin adjunction, then
$$\eta_{C_SK}^p=C_V(\eta_K^e),$$
under $C_V(\pi_e^*K\otimes_A^LL_V(d)[2d])\cong L\pi_p^*C_SK(d)[2d]$ and $C_V\pi^{\times,e}K\cong R\pi^!C_SK$. The inverse of this transported map is the vector-bundle identification specified by [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity]. All these comparisons are independent of the annihilating exponent $r$. No divisibility of $n$ by the ramification index, and no flatness of $A$ over $\mathbf Z/\ell^r$, is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09AF, lemma-jshriek-comparison, and Tag 099R, section-comparison; combined with categories.tex Tag 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints. Agent-written comparison of the specific Kummer-normalized maps of blueprint sk-prop-sf-cbc/def-amb-p1-trace and sk-prop-an/thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity; the class comparison alone does not assert this map comparison.

proof.text:
A field is Noetherian: its ideals are zero and the whole field. Thus $S$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The same holds for the finite-type schemes in the vector-bundle coordinate towers and their projective compactifications; finite type is checked in the finite affine trivializing cover, where the algebras are polynomial algebras or their standard projective charts. Every trivializing open and every overlap is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]; overlaps need not be affine. By [def-weil-proper-morphism], every proper map is separated and finite type: it is quasi-compact, and its diagonal is a closed immersion, hence quasi-compact. Thus these maps are quasi-separated as well, and the named direct-image comparison applies. Every input to that comparison will be bounded below.

Write $C_T=\nu_T^*$. By [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact], $C_T$ is exact and additive, identifies constant rings, and commutes with cohomology. By [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] it commutes with scheme inverse images, with their identity and composition constraints. The natural derived tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] gives $C_T(F\otimes_A^LG)\cong C_TF\otimes_A^LC_TG$. The unital and shift-compatible structures are those of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. We use these specified comparisons throughout; additivity identifies finite biproducts and exactness identifies shifts.

source.place: Tag 099R, section-comparison; coefficient and tensor bookkeeping for the finite-level comparison

proof.text:
Put $R=\mathbf Z/\ell^r$ and $M_T=\varprojlim_s\mu_{\ell^s,T}^{\mathrm{proet}}$. Clauses (1) and (2) of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] give a rank-one $R$-line $\mu_{\ell^r}$ and the projection-induced identification $M_T/\ell^rM_T\cong\mu_{\ell^r,T}^{\mathrm{proet}}$. Tensor associativity in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] gives, using $\ell^rA=0$,
$$A_T(1)=M_T\otimes_{(\mathbf Z_\ell)_T}A_T
\cong(M_T/\ell^rM_T)\otimes_{R_T}A_T
\cong\mu_{\ell^r,T}^{\mathrm{proet}}\otimes_{R_T}A_T.$$
The comparison of the etale roots with these pro-etale roots is the one in [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map]. Its inverse projection identification is precisely $\tau_T:C_TL_T\to A_T(1)$. There is no higher derived tensor contribution: $\mu_{\ell^r}^{\mathrm{et}}$ is locally free of rank one by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], so it, rather than $A$, is the flat factor.

For $w:T'\to T$, pullback of a compatible root sequence sends its $s$th coordinate $z_s$ to the pulled-back root $w^*z_s$; hence $w^*p_r=p_r w^*$ for the projection $p_r$. The root comparison of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] is an isomorphism for every such $w$. Applying the displayed quotient-and-tensor formulas proves naturality of $\tau$, and taking tensor powers proves it for $d\geq0$. In degree $d=0$ these are the constant-ring unit comparisons. If $s\geq r$ also kills $A$, then $p_r=(z\mapsto z^{\ell^{s-r}})p_s$. Tensoring this equality with $A$ proves equality of the two identifications under the transition isomorphism in [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Any two annihilating exponents have a common larger exponent. This proves independence of $r$ without commuting inverse image with an infinite limit and without assuming $A$ flat over $R$.

source.place: Tag 099R, section-comparison; projection from the roots-of-unity tower, as specified by lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map; agent-written naturality calculation

proof.text:
For a quasi-compact quasi-separated $u:U\to T$, put $l=u_e^*$, $r_u=Ru_{e,*}$, $p=Lu_p^*$ and $s_u=Ru_{p,*}$, and write $a:C_Ul\cong pC_T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate], $\beta_u:C_Tr_u\to s_uC_U$ is the mate with counit equation
$$\varepsilon^p\,p(\beta_u)\,a=C_U(\varepsilon^e).$$
Consequently for every $v:lB\to F$ with adjunct $\widehat v:B\to r_uF$, the adjunct of $C_U(v)a_B^{-1}$ is $\beta_{u,F}C_T(\widehat v)$. Indeed $v=\varepsilon_F^e\,l(\widehat v)$; substitute this expression and the displayed counit equation and then use naturality of $a$. The resulting expression is $\varepsilon^p_{C_UF}\,p(\beta_{u,F}C_T\widehat v)$, which is the inverse Hom-bijection formula. Taking $v=1_{lB}$ gives the corresponding unit equation. This argument uses only the explicit mate bijection [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], and compares the actual units, classes and maps.

source.place: Tag 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints; explicit Hom-bijection calculation for the specified square

proof.text:
Apply Step 3 to $u=q:\mathbf P^1_S\to S$. The infinity divisor is Cartier: on the chart at infinity its ideal is generated by the polynomial coordinate, a nonzerodivisor in a polynomial ring over any base ring. The transition of its dual ideal is the transition of $\mathcal O(1)$. The statement of [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] identifies the composite $A_P\to i_*A_S\to A_P(1)[2]$ with the scalar-extended etale Kummer first Chern class of $\mathcal O_P(1)$ under $C_P$ and $\tau_P$. Its adjoint is therefore $\beta_qC_S(h_q^e)=h_q^p$ by Step 3. The same step's unit equation identifies the other component, the shifted twisted unit. Thus, comparing both biproduct components,
$$\beta_qC_S(b_q^e)=b_q^p.$$
By [def-amb-p1-trace], $b_q^e$ is invertible and $t_q^e=\operatorname{pr}_2(b_q^e)^{-1}$. Applying a functor preserves both inverse equations, so $b_q^p$ is invertible. Inverting the preceding equality and composing with $\operatorname{pr}_2$ gives $t_q^p\beta_q=C_S(t_q^e)$. Finally $h_q^p=b_q^p\iota_2$ gives $t_q^ph_q^p=\operatorname{pr}_2\iota_2=1$. These are equations between the Kummer-normalized maps; no choice of a decomposition or scalar is made.

source.place: Projective-line normalization via sk-prop-sf-cbc/def-amb-p1-trace; combine the two components using Steps 2–3

proof.text: Let $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ be an open immersion. The canonical map $e_j:C_Tj_!^e\cong j_!^pC_U$ of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] is the adjoint comparison, as Stacks Tag 09AF constructs it. Explicitly, after restriction to $U$, it is the identity on $C_UF$ under $j^*j_!F=F$. The counit $j_!j^*G\to G$ is likewise the adjoint of $1_{j^*G}$: on sections lying in $U$ it is the identity, as [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] specifies. The pro-etale adjunction is [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. Thus, under the pullback comparison $a_j$, both routes from $C_Tj_!^ej_e^*G$ to $C_TG$ have the same adjunct, the identity of $j_p^*C_TG$, and are equal. Exactness of $C$ and of both extensions by zero [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact, lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact] gives the identical equation termwise on complexes and after localization. In particular, for $U=\mathbf A^1_S$, $T=P$, naturality of $\beta_q$ and Step 4 identify $Rq_*j_!j^*L_P[2]\to Rq_*L_P[2]\xrightarrow{t_q}A_S$ on the two sites. This proves the asserted comparison of restricted line traces, including the counit used for the restriction.

proof.text:
For a chosen compactification $f=\bar f j$, set
$$B_f=R\bar f_{p,*}(e_j)\circ\beta_{\bar f,j_!}:C_YR\bar f_{e,*}j_!^e\longrightarrow R\bar f_{p,*}j_!^pC_X.$$
Both factors are invertible by Steps 3 and 5. For the projective completion of $V$ this is exactly the $\beta_\pi$ in the statement, not a replacement isomorphism. We need its compatibility with the compact-support composition and restriction maps used in the local construction. Here are the named-map checks. Direct-image comparison respects composition by [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image], and open-extension comparison respects composition by [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]. A proper refinement contributes the proper/open map and its inverse; their site-comparison equation is exactly [lem-sf-proper-open-comparison-site-normalization]. A restriction square contributes the direct-image exchange and the open-extension base-change map. The first is compared by [lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange]; the second is compared by taking its adjoint, where both are the same pullback-composition identity, just as in Step 5. For a proper/open interchange in a compatible compactification tower, let its square have top open $k:U\hookrightarrow W$, bottom open $i:T\hookrightarrow Z$, and proper verticals $r:U\to T$, $p:W\to Z$. A merely commutative square need not be Cartesian. Use the finite-evaluation normalization in [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]: take its coefficient ring $B=A$, the constant strict tower with value $C_UL$, all transition maps identities, and at each level the finite ring $\Lambda_n=A$ and witness $L_n=L\in D^+(U_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Its evaluation clause identifies the specified pro-etale proper/open comparison with the image of the normalized etale comparison of [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence] under precisely the direct-image and open-extension comparisons fixed here. More explicitly, put $W_T=W\times_ZT$, with maps $b:W_T\to W$, $q:W_T\to T$, and $s=(k,r):U\to W_T$. The cited calculus states that $s$ is clopen. Its comparison is the proper-adjunction mate of $p^*i_!\to b_!q^*\to b_!s_!s^*q^*\cong k_!r^*$, where the first arrow is open base change and the second is projection onto the clopen component $s(U)$. The projection is identity on $s(U)$ and zero on its complementary open. Exact comparison preserves these two maps. Together with the counit equations in Step 3 and the open-adjunction equations in Step 5, the mate formula compares this actual proper/open arrow. The finite-evaluation clause ensures that this mate has the prescribed etale normalization; no faithfulness of derived evaluation is needed. Pasting these squares compares a whole tower, by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] (1)–(2). In particular the etale and pro-etale composition maps of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] and [thm-sf-comp-composition] give
$$B_{gf}\,C(\alpha^e_{g,f})=\alpha^p_{g,f}\,(Rg_!^p B_f)\,(B_g Rf_!^e),$$
with the indicated whiskerings and site identifications. The same computation gives compatibility with restriction to any trivializing open. Invertibility of the restriction exchange on the inputs here follows from [thm-cbc-finite-torsion] and [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale]; all inputs have the displayed bounded-below etale witnesses. Thus one can compute with the ordered tower compactification and return to the projective completion without changing $B_f$.

source.place: Tags 099R (section-comparison) and 09AF (lemma-jshriek-comparison); canonical compactification comparisons and mate pasting, agent-written verification

proof.text:
We now compare the projection maps, rather than deducing them from equality of the traces. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] to the commutative square of ringed topoi with upper horizontal $\nu_{\overline V}$, lower horizontal $\nu_S$, and vertical maps $\bar\pi_p,\bar\pi_e$. The structure rings are the constant ring $A$; Step 1 identifies their inverse images, so this is a ringed square. Its exchange is exactly $\beta_{\bar\pi}$ by Step 3. The statement of that tensor-coherence lemma says that exchange identifies the proper projection maps defined as the mates of counit tensor identity. Thus it compares the actual proper-piece arrows, without any perfectness or Tor assumption on this formal equality. For the open piece, compare first the inverse projection arrow $\kappa:j_!(F\otimes^L j^*G)\to (j_!F)\otimes^L G$. Under $j_!\dashv j^*$ its adjunct is the tensor of the unit $F\to j^*j_!F$ with $1_{j^*G}$, followed by the inverse of the tensor-pullback comparison. This is a correctly typed adjunct because the source is $j_!(F\otimes^L j^*G)$. Write $\gamma:(j_!F)\otimes^L G\to j_!(F\otimes^L j^*G)$ for the forward canonical arrow. Its restriction is the identity under $j^*j_!=1$. Consequently $\gamma\kappa=1$: under the open adjunction both sides have the same adjunct, the unit of $F\otimes^L j^*G$. On the pro-etale site $\gamma$ is invertible by [lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula], so $\kappa=\gamma^{-1}$. Step 5 compares the open adjunctions and their units, and Step 1 compares their tensor-pullback maps. Hence applying $C$ carries the specified etale adjunct to the specified pro-etale adjunct, and compares $\kappa$ itself. On the inputs here, $G$ is bounded below (in particular the stated finite-Tor $K$ is bounded), and $F$ is a rank-one twist with a shift, so $H=F\otimes^L j^*G$ and $j_!H$ are bounded below. At this intermediate point use the termwise exact comparison on the unbounded derived categories of [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], before restricting it to $D^+$: its tensor comparison from Step 1 identifies $C((j_!F)\otimes^L G)$ with $(j_!C F)\otimes^L C G$. The pro-etale projection isomorphism identifies this with $j_!C H$, hence it is bounded below. This also proves that the etale tensor target is bounded below: by Step 1 its cohomology pulls back to the corresponding pro-etale cohomology, and faithfulness on degree-zero sheaves in [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] reflects the vanishing. Full faithfulness on $D^+$ now reflects invertibility of $\kappa$: lift the inverse of $C(\kappa)$ and use faithfulness on its two inverse equations. Thus $\kappa$ is also invertible on the etale site; $\gamma\kappa=1$ identifies its inverse with the specified etale forward arrow. Taking inverses now compares the actual forward open-piece arrows.

The compact-support projection transformation is the proper-piece arrow followed by this open-piece arrow, exactly as [def-exchange-projection] specifies; the ordinary etale proper map is the counit-mate map of [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. Composing the two checked squares compares the compact-support projection maps via $B_\pi$. On the inputs $L_V(d)[2d]$ and $K$ in the question, invertibility is [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula]: the twist is a finite rank-one local system by Step 2, and $K$ is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude. Taking inverses therefore also compares the displayed projection isomorphisms in the direction used by $a_K$.

proof.text:
We compare the ordered affine-space traces by induction on $d$. For $d=0$, compact support is the identity and the trace is $1_A$, on both sites. For $d=1$, the equality is Step 5. Suppose it holds for $d-1$. In the coordinate tower write $p_d=p_{d-1}u$, with $u$ the last affine-line projection. The composite-counit formula [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] says that its counit is the outer counit composed with the outer left adjoint applied to the inner counit. This is exactly how [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] specifies the ordered integration. Apply $C$ to this two-factor composite. For the inner line counit with the remaining twist-and-shift as coefficient, the projection comparison already proved in Step 7 identifies its projection factor; its trace factor is the line trace from Step 5. The coefficient is a finite rank-one local system with a shift, so it satisfies the bounded constructible finite-Tor hypotheses of Step 7. Step 5 compares the inner line trace, the inductive hypothesis compares the outer trace, and Step 6 compares the intervening compact-support composition maps. The tensor and pullback identifications from Steps 1–2 identify the sum of the twists and shifts. Hence
$$t_{p_d}^p B_{p_d}=C_S(t_{p_d}^e).$$
The etale trace is an isomorphism by [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace]; therefore so is the pro-etale trace. This also proves that its source has cohomology only in degree zero, where it is $A_S$.

source.place: Ordered coordinate tower; identity adjunction at d=0 and explicit induction using the composite counit

proof.text:
Choose a finite trivializing open cover $\{U_i\}$ of the vector bundle. On $U_{ij}$ the coordinate changes are invertible matrices in $\operatorname{GL}_d(\mathcal O_S(U_{ij}))$, as [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section] states. The etale trace is invariant under these changes by [lem-amb-linear-trace-invariance]. Naturality of $B_\pi$ in its input and its restriction compatibility from Step 6 identify the two pro-etale coordinate traces with the images of the same etale trace by Step 8; in particular they agree on $U_{ij}$. This also explains why frame changes act on the compact-support source by the compared maps: a coordinate isomorphism extends to projective completion by $[x_0:x]\mapsto[x_0:Gx]$, with inverse given by $G^{-1}$, and is proper; use the proper/refinement and direct-image composition comparisons in Step 6 on its extension to the projective completion. Both sides are bounded below.

Put $M^e=R\pi_!^eL_V(d)[2d]$ and $M^p=R\pi_!^pA_V(d)[2d]$. The restriction comparison and Step 8 give $M^p|_{U_i}\cong A_{U_i}[0]$, and the analogous assertion for $M^e$. Exact open restriction commutes with $\ker d/\operatorname{im}d$ [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. The sheaf uniqueness axiom on this cover thus implies $\mathcal H^a(M^p)=\mathcal H^a(M^e)=0$ for $a\ne0$. The good-truncation definitions [def-kun-truncations] give functorial quasi-isomorphisms $M\leftarrow\tau_{\leq0}M\to\mathcal H^0(M)[0]$ for either $M$. These induce the canonical identifications in the derived category and commute with restrictions. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] the local traces correspond to actual sheaf maps $\mathcal H^0(M)|_{U_i}\to A_{U_i}$. Their overlap equalities glue uniquely by [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing]. This constructs the asserted global $t_\pi^p$. The same argument and [def-amb-vector-integration] identify $t_\pi^e$ with the etale glued trace. After the degree-zero identifications both $t_\pi^p B_\pi$ and $C_S(t_\pi^e)$ are sheaf maps agreeing on the cover by Step 8, hence
$$t_\pi^p\beta_\pi=C_S(t_\pi^e).$$
This is gluing of sheaf maps; no descent assertion for arbitrary derived morphisms is used.

source.place: Frame invariance and gluing paragraph; supplied truncation argument making the degree-zero sheaf descent explicit

proof.text:
Set $J=\pi_e^*K\otimes_A^LL_V(d)[2d]$. It is bounded below; Step 2 identifies $C_VJ$ with $L\pi_p^*C_SK(d)[2d]$. Step 7 compares the projection factors of $a$, and Step 9 compares the traces in their second factors. Bifunctoriality of tensor therefore gives the actual equality
$$a_{C_SK}^p\,B_{\pi,J}=C_S(a_K^e).$$
To compute its transpose, use [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] and [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. The vector-bundle projection is separated and finite type, and its projective completion is proper over $S$. All these schemes are finite type over the fixed algebraic closure $k$ of the finite field. By [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], the finite-type $k$-scheme $\overline V$ has finite dimension. Choose an integer bound $D$ for that dimension; in particular it bounds the fiber dimensions of the proper compactification. Apply the ambient-adjoint-class statement with bound $D$, independently of the vector-bundle rank $d$. If $S$ is empty all asserted maps are the unique maps between zero objects. Its bounded-below etale-origin hypothesis holds for $C_VJ$, and the target $C_SK$ is bounded below by Step 1. For a bounded-below etale $J$ and etale $K$ the transported Hom-bijection is the composite
$$\operatorname{Hom}_p(R\pi_!^pC_VJ,C_SK)
\xrightarrow{\ -\circ B_{\pi,J}\ }\operatorname{Hom}_p(C_SR\pi_!^eJ,C_SK)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_e(R\pi_!^eJ,K)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_e(J,\pi^{\times,e}K)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_p(C_VJ,C_V\pi^{\times,e}K).$$
The first comparison is the explicit compactification comparison of Step 6. The last uses that $\pi^{\times,e}K$ is bounded below here: [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity] identifies it with $J$. The comparison unit $K\to R\nu_*C_SK$ in [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] identifies the last target with $R\pi^!C_SK$ as defined in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Under this displayed chain the already proved equality sends $a_{C_SK}^p$ to the etale map $a_K^e$, then to $\eta_K^e$, and then to $C_V(\eta_K^e)$. Hence the claimed equality of transposes follows, with exactly the source and target comparisons stated in the question. This calculation uses the bounded etale-origin adjunction, not an ambient pro-etale exceptional adjunction on all complexes.

The map $\eta_K^e$ is invertible by [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity]. Apply $C_V$ to its two inverse equations. Step 10 identifies its image with $\eta_{C_SK}^p$, so that map is invertible and its inverse is the transported inverse of the integration adjoint. This is precisely the vector-bundle identification named in the statement: [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity] is used with the integration-adjoint normalization specified by the ordinary vector-bundle theorem and the definition of the transported exceptional inverse image. The equality has been proved for the maps themselves before taking inverses.

Step 2 shows equality of the twist comparisons for two annihilating exponents after passage to a common larger one, and [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] gives the same independence for the Kummer class. Thus the two $h_q$ are equal. The other component is the unit, so the two $b_q$ are equal, their inverses and traces are equal, and their restrictions are equal by Step 5. Induction in Step 8 makes the affine-space maps equal. Uniqueness for the sheaf gluing in Step 9 makes the vector integrations equal. Finally the projection maps and the Hom-bijection in Steps 7 and 10 use no exponent, so their composites and transposes are equal. This proves every claimed exponent independence. The identity case $d=0$, the empty base, and ramified $A$ with $e(E/\mathbf Q_\ell)\nmid n$ require no change: only the existence of an annihilating $\ell^r$ and the flatness of the root line, not freeness or flatness of $A$ over $\mathbf Z/\ell^r$, entered the proof.
